audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect flags a real contradiction: winRate has Poppy at 52.81% (owner favored) but content win[] gives Seraphine 6 of 7 rows and full phases[].side is a flat 'Skill' template on all 7. The content-layer whys[] array is itself internally split (whys[4] argues Poppy wins level 6, but win[4]='Seraphine'; whys[5] argues Seraphine wins first item, but win[5]='Poppy') — the two prose sources in the same file disagree with each other and with the packet-derived win rate.
audit.why: Nothing in either kit resolves which of the three conflicting sources (win[], whys[], win-rate) is correct, so moving phases[].side to match win[] would just propagate an already-contradicted array, and moving it to match the win rate would fight the mirror side's already-approved chart (seraphine_sup__poppy.json moved 6 of 7 rows to Seraphine).
audit.corrected: Left phases[].side and win[] untouched per the contradiction-guard rule. Recorded here instead of guessing.

audit.why: spikes[] correctly names level 2 Q High Note poke outranging melee, level 6 R Keeper's Verdict as the all-in window, first-item W Surround Sound reclaiming the 2v2, and late-game R Encore chain-charm.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names Beat Drop as matchup-defining but carries no cooldown number (lint: COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT), and omits that Beat Drop (E) or Encore (R) landing mid-cast cancels Poppy's Keeper's Verdict channel outright (missingInteractions: your-channel-punished).
audit.why: Beat Drop is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s by rank; a real number lets the reader time an R channel around it, and the channel-cancel is the single most punishable interaction in the matchup.
audit.corrected: Added rank-1/rank-5 Beat Drop cooldown and the channel-cancel interaction to breakdown.cooldowns.
